title: Local inference notebook / lightweight harness brainstorm
content:
Context / why this exists:
- We need a super-light, reproducible way for engineers/product folks to iterate on prompts, small model variants, and routing logic without spinning up cloud Dedicated instances or using hosted tokens.
- Current local flow is messy: ad-hoc notebooks, different env vars, inefficient caching. Slow onboarding for new hires and PMs who want to validate a behavior quickly.

Core idea (one-liner):
- A tiny cross-platform notebook + CLI harness that can: emulate token cost, simulate latency bands, swap model artifacts (quantized vs fp16), and capture prompt-level telemetry.

Primary constraints / non-goals:
- NOT trying to fully mirror production (no complex batch scheduling, no autoscaling emulation).
- Should be safe for PII: default offline artifacts only; if using hosted creds we show a big warning and mask logs.
- Keep dependencies minimal (python-only or node optional).

Persona / users:
- FE dev building chat UI who wants to test prompt changes quickly.
- PM/PMM validating quality tradeoffs between two prompts/model knobs.
- SRE/infra person debugging a latency regression locally.

Key features (minimal viable set):
1) Quick start notebook template: single-file Jupyter / Colab notebook with helper cells: load model (local weight path OR light hosted proxy), run prompt, visualize tokenization, show token/time/cost estimate.
2) CLI harness: run a prompt file (-p prompt.txt) with options: --model PATH, --quantized, --latency-ms 50, --cost-multiplier 1.2, --session-id. Outputs JSON with timing and token breakdown.
3) Cost/latency simulator: simple pluggable modules to add fixed latency, jitter, and per-token cost models to mimic hosted pricing.
4) Snapshot capture: record input prompt, model config, raw output, token metrics, and a short diff view for successive runs. Store as local JSON artifacts for quick diffs.
5) Lightweight telemetry UI: small HTML reporter (static) that reads snapshots and surfaces regressions or quality drops.
6) Privacy first defaults: clear prompts sanitized, file-based key store with optional redaction.

User stories / acceptance notes (rough):
- As a frontend dev, I can run `local-harness run --prompt examples/checkout.txt --model ~/models/3b-q8.bin` and get a single JSON with latency, tokens_in, tokens_out, and cost_estimate within 5s.
- As a PM, I can point the notebook at two snapshot files and see a % change on token usage and a small diff view of outputs.
- As an infra engineer, I can simulate a 300ms tail latency and verify UI fallback behavior end-to-end by piping harness output through local mock server.

Success metrics (for an initial alpha):
- Onboard a 3-person eng+pm team in < 30 minutes from repo clone to first snapshot.
- >80% of prompt iter sessions use the harness instead of ad-hoc notebooks (measured via local git commit tags or opt-in telemetry).
- Time-to-iterate on a prompt reduces by 40% (informal survey).

Rough UX / commands (brainstorm):
- Setup: `pip install -r requirements.txt` or `npm i -g redwood-local-harness` (goal keep both tiny).
- CLI examples:
  - `lh run --prompt example/prompts/onboarding.txt --model local:3b-q8 --latency 80 --out snapshots/run1.json`
  - `lh compare snapshots/run1.json snapshots/run2.json --report html --open`
- Notebook has cells: env check, load model, run prompt, visualize tokens, snapshot results.

Privacy / security checklist (notes):
- Default snapshot folder is .redwood-local (gitignored) and encrypted with passphrase on first use.
- If user supplies hosted API key, require explicit `--hosted-ack` flag and produce a redacted snapshot copy removing email-like tokens.

Implementation notes / prototyping plan:
- Phase 0 (week 0-1): PoC CLI wrapper around vLLM or llama.cpp to load local small models and produce token/timing. Minimal simulator for latency/cost.
- Phase 1 (week 2-4): Notebook templates + snapshot format (JSON schema). Add compare tool and HTML reporter.
- Phase 2 (week 5-8): Add quick hosted-proxy mode, telemetry opt-in, small UX polish.

Data / format choices:
- Snapshot JSON fields: { run_id, created_at, prompt_sha, model_name, model_path, quantized, tokens_in, tokens_out, per_token_cost, total_cost, timings: {cold_ms, token_ms_avg, tail_ms}, output_text, redacted:bool }
- Keep schema flat to make diffs easy. (We will not nest deep structures.)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best estimate tokenization for different tokenizers? (Use tiktoken for main languages, fallback heuristics for others)
- Should harness support multi-turn session emulation or just single-turn? (Start single-turn; session mode v2)
- Where to host example model binaries for onboarding? (Small quantized test models in GH LFS or a public artifact bucket)
- How opinionated about cost model? (Provide default Redwood hosted-like numbers, allow overrides)

Related references / quick links:
- JIRA: DEVX-4823 (placeholder for GH integration)
- GH: repo/local-runner (proto)
- Slack thread: #devx-local-harness (flag idea request)

Notes to self (fragmentary):
- MVP should require zero cloud creds. If user has them, warn loudly.
- Think about adding a tiny web UI that can replay the snapshot as a mock stream for FE testing.
- Could be a good 2-week hackathon project for new grads.

Possible future expansions (parking lot):
- Multi-turn session recording + replay with simulated KV cache decay.
- Batch-run tool to measure token-cost across 100 prompts to estimate cost saving from caching/compaction.
- Integration with Redwood Console to upload anonymized snapshots for product fuzz testing.

Bottom line: build something fast and boring first — CLI + notebook + snapshot/compare — keep it local and privacy-first.

----

End of brainstorm notes.
